subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration is the change in velocity per second, so its unit is metres per second squared (m/s²).

questions.q: Which equation correctly defines acceleration, where u is initial velocity and v is final velocity?
questions.explain: Acceleration equals the change in velocity (v − u) divided by the time taken (t).

questions.q: How does velocity differ from speed?
options: Velocity is speed in a given direction
Velocity is always larger than speed
questions.explain: Velocity is a vector quantity: it is speed together with a specified direction.

questions.q: Which equation links final velocity (v), initial velocity (u), acceleration (a) and distance (s)?
questions.explain: The equation v² = u² + 2as relates velocities, acceleration and distance without needing time.

questions.q: A typical value for the average speed of a person walking is closest to which of these?
questions.explain: An adult walking has an average speed of roughly 1.5 m/s.

questions.q: What does the gradient (slope) of a distance-time graph represent?
questions.explain: On a distance-time graph the gradient gives the speed of the object.

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
questions.explain: The area beneath a velocity-time graph equals the distance travelled by the object.

questions.q: A distance-time graph shows a horizontal (flat) line. What is the object doing?
options: It is moving at constant speed
questions.explain: A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means the distance is not changing, so the object is stationary.

questions.q: Two objects are shown on the same distance-time graph. What does a steeper gradient indicate?
questions.explain: A steeper gradient on a distance-time graph means a greater speed.

questions.q: What does a horizontal (flat) line on a velocity-time graph show?
questions.explain: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means velocity is unchanging, so the object moves at constant velocity.

questions.q: What does the gradient of a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explain: The gradient of a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration of the object.

questions.q: Which equation states Newton's second law of motion?
questions.explain: Newton's second law gives resultant force as mass multiplied by acceleration (F = ma).

questions.q: Which statement best describes Newton's first law?
options: An object stays at rest or moves at constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
questions.explain: Newton's first law states motion only changes when a resultant (unbalanced) force acts.

questions.q: A car travels at a steady velocity along a straight road. What is the resultant force on it?
options: Equal to the driving force only
questions.explain: Constant velocity means balanced forces, so the resultant force is zero (Newton's first law).

questions.q: Which is a correct example of Newton's third law?
options: A swimmer pushes water backwards and the water pushes the swimmer forwards
A heavier object accelerates less for the same force
A moving object slows down due to friction
A falling object speeds up as it falls
questions.explain: Newton's third law: when two objects interact they exert equal and opposite forces on each other.

questions.q: For a fixed resultant force, what happens to acceleration if the mass of an object increases?
questions.explain: From F = ma, for a fixed force a larger mass gives a smaller acceleration.

questions.q: The stopping distance of a vehicle is the sum of which two distances?
questions.explain: Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance.

questions.q: Which factor would increase a driver's thinking distance?
options: Being tired or having drunk alcohol
questions.explain: Thinking distance depends on reaction time, which is increased by tiredness, alcohol, drugs or distractions.

questions.q: Which factor increases the braking distance of a car?
options: A wet or icy road surface
questions.explain: Braking distance is increased by poor road conditions, worn tyres or brakes, and greater speed or mass.

questions.q: A car travels 100 m in 5 s at constant speed. What is its speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 m/s.

questions.q: A car speeds up from rest to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration = (v − u) ÷ t = (20 − 0) ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

questions.q: A resultant force acts on a 2 kg mass, giving it an acceleration of 3 m/s². What is the size of the force?
